A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TEAL research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably across the added appendix sections and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original activation analyses, perplexity and downstream-task evaluations, and kernel and decoding-speed measurements. Appendix A.2 supplies detailed task results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds the authors' MaskLLM training and evaluation in A.4 and LoRA fine-tuning experiments in A.5. The separately cited MaskLLM speedup is distinguished from these original experiments.

M1.justification: The magnitude-thresholding procedure, greedy sparsity allocation and sparse kernel remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 introduces an optional LoRA fine-tuning extension, whereas v2 only discussed sparse-aware adaptation as future work.

E1.justification: C4, WikiText and the six downstream tasks are retained, with no added data domain or task requirement. A.4 and A.5 use already-covered models and datasets under additional compression and fine-tuning configurations.

E2.justification: v3 removes the training-free ReLUfication comparator row from Table 1 and its baseline description, while retaining CATS. A.4 adds an evaluated MaskLLM 2:4 weight-sparsity comparator and a combined TEAL–MaskLLM configuration. This is a limited extension of the comparison set.

E3.justification: New appendix protocols include training MaskLLM masks on 2B C4 tokens and comparing LoRA fine-tuning on 30M C4 tokens against no fine-tuning at 50%, 60%, 70% and 90% sparsity. Existing evaluation settings, including 128 language-modeling samples, 2048-token context, 512-token evaluation window and downstream few-shot settings, are retained.

E4.justification: A.4 newly tests combining activation sparsity with 2:4 weight sparsity, and A.5 tests whether fine-tuning recovers performance as sparsity increases. The existing input-versus-output, greedy-versus-uniform, quantization, prefill and batch-size analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new appendix tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing TEAL/CATS scores and all figure data are retained, but six ReLUfication perplexities disappear from Table 1. A.4 adds MaskLLM and combined-method perplexities of 8.532 and 9.590, and juxtaposes the retained TEAL 1.78x speedup with a cited MaskLLM 1.4x value. Table 10 adds fine-tuning results, including 13.39 without versus 9.927 with fine-tuning at 70% sparsity. These are additional conditions, not improved results for the unchanged v2 procedure.

T1.justification: Definition 1 and Appendix A.1's Gaussian assumptions, definitions, lemmas, theorem and proofs are unchanged. A.3 supplies background architecture explanation and reexpresses the previously stated SwiGLU computation without adding a substantive theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of training-free 40–50% model-wide sparsity, limited accuracy degradation, speedups up to 1.53x and 1.8x, and compatibility with quantization. The appendix additions do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: A.4 newly interprets activation and weight sparsity as complementary and qualifies its speed comparison because 2:4 sparsity can better serve high-batch and prefill workloads. A.5 presents fine-tuning as partial recovery from aggressive sparsification. The original applications and batch-scaling limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly discloses roughly five input tokens and at most 200 generated tokens for the existing GPT-Fast benchmark; this does not establish a protocol change. A.4 reports approximately 800 H100 hours for MaskLLM training, while A.5 specifies LoRA rank 32, learning rate 0.0002, approximately 1% trainable parameters and 30M C4 tokens. The code-access reference is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion and citations for converting dense models into MoE models. Additional references include MaskLLM, LoRA, GQA and BitDelta, and the C4 citation changes from Dodge et al. to Raffel et al. A.4 modestly broadens positioning against weight sparsity while preserving the main comparison with CATS.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized edits to baseline descriptions and algorithm comments, adds the architecture overview in A.3 and appendix subsections A.4–A.5, and introduces acknowledgments and the ICLR publication header. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds two unnumbered tables in A.4 and Table 10, removes the ReLUfication row from Table 1, and expands Figure 3's caption to explain its existing theoretical-optimum line. All ten figure images are retained, with minor resizing and reflow; existing appendix tables move without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: The new MaskLLM and LoRA experiments provide useful evidence about combining sparsity methods and recovering accuracy, while the decoding-length disclosure improves reproducibility. The gains are limited: the MaskLLM latency comparison uses a cited value, and removing ReLUfication's quantitative results while retaining its degeneration claim reduces transparency slightly. Overall, the additional evidence and documentation modestly improve an otherwise stable paper.
